To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a new deep learning system for medical coding that outperforms the previous state of the art on the MIMIC dataset and that our system’s performance is significantly enhanced by the use of multi-view convolutional channels and attention regularization mediated by natural-language descriptions.

we propose a novel attention regularization method for label-dependent attention and a novel multi-view convolutional architecture for medical code prediction, and that we achieve state-of-the-art results on the MIMIC dataset.

(1) multiview convolutions are an effective way of learning kernel size adjustments for natural language processing, (2) description regularization is an effective way of addressing sparsity in label space for natural language processing and (3) our system, which combines these two novel techniques with other recent advances, achieves a new best result for the MIMC-III task.

improving the state of the practice of deep learning in healthcare.

we have proposed an effective method for automated coding of medical records, and we have also provided insights for further improvements.

the system we propose can be seen as a combination of two main ideas: (1) the use of a multi-view convolutional network to process the input data, which is a novel approach to deal with the problem of long and heterogeneous medical reports, and (2) the use of attention mechanisms and regularization terms that allow to deal with the sparsity problem that exists in this dataset.
